newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mazda sees no need for more Ford equity investment.
newsitem.headline: Mazda sees no need for more Ford equity investment.

text.p: Mazda Motor Corp President Henry Wallace told Reuters on Thursday that he did not see any need to receive additional financial support from Ford Motor Co in the form of further equity investment.
In April 1996 Ford raised its stake in Mazda to one-third from about one-fourth, giving it management control of the Japanese carmaker.
Soon after that, Wallace took over as Mazda's president and took up the task of pulling the troubled company out of the red.
Wallace said in an interview that Mazda may need to do some refinancing in the future, but he did not see any reason why the company would need to increase its capital.
He added that Mazda is looking to reduce its debt burden.
Wallace added that he did not know Ford's intentions on the issue of equity investments in Mazda and that he had held no discussions with Ford on the issue.
